newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel unlinked bonds finish higher.
newsitem.headline: Israel unlinked bonds finish higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher on Tuesday as investors believe annual inflation will not be as high as expected and therefore interest rates will remain high, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.10 pct to 168.57
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct at 159.56
Volume was strong at 166 million shekels with inflation-linked bonds falling for the fourth consecutive session, traders said.
"Most of the activity was in the unlinked bonds. The Gilons are showing nice yields of 16.5-16.6 percent," said Dan Lallouz, a portfolio manager at Clal Insurance.

"The unlinked bonds are very attractive now. The inflation figure is expected to be around nine percent. This means that yields are relatively high," said Amir Eayal, head of portfolio management at Epsilon Securities.
CPI-linked bonds continued to decline after a strong price run-up in the last two months.

"Inflation-linked long bonds continued to fall, but the decline was moderate today. The fact that the Bank of Israel plans to resume issuing linked bonds (after a lapse of several months) is putting pressure on the long bonds," Lallouz said.
The Makams (which are unlinked) closed almost unchanged with most of the activity concentrated in the short series.
"The dollar-linked bonds closed lower after the decline of dollar (against the shekel) on Monday. Activity in these bonds continues to be very low," Eyal said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
